strengths: The paper identifies a useful problem: interpretable macro-level features can be confounded with model predictions even when predictions are deterministic functions of pixels. This distinction has an identifiable audience in explainability and causal discovery.

Using FCI and partial ancestral graphs is a principled way to represent latent confounding and unresolved causal directions. The background constraint that predictions cannot cause input features is well motivated, and the discussion acknowledges faithfulness, limited identifiability, and dependence on expert-selected features.

The manuscript is generally readable, with helpful graphical examples, an illustrative simulation with an omitted feature, and two applications. The preprocessing appendix and bootstrap summaries make the proposed workflow concrete. Applying established causal discovery tools is an appropriate contribution; a new algorithm is not required.
weaknesses: Necessary: the empirical causal interpretations exceed what the reported summaries establish. Section 6.3 combines directed and circle-arrow edges, although a consistently recovered circle-arrow edge can remain compatible with entirely confounded dependence. Such stability does not establish that a feature is a likely cause. Furthermore, absence of an edge directly into the prediction does not exclude indirect causation: Figure 10 contains a possible path from Cardiomegaly through Atelectasis to the prediction. Report definite and possible ancestry separately, include confounded relationships, and correct the captions and statements that other features are not causally relevant.

Necessary: address selection bias in the X-ray experiment. Section 6.1 selects pneumonia cases and controls specifically having 'no findings', making inclusion depend on the outcome and the explanatory findings. This can induce dependencies through selection, yet Section 3 treats selection bias as irrelevant and the assumed model does not represent this sampling mechanism. The manuscript needs to justify why the causal interpretations survive this selection, revise the analysis, or withdraw the affected causal conclusions.

Necessary: establish the reliability of the conditional independence tests used for the applications. Chi-square testing with 26 multilevel bird attributes and conditioning sets up to size four can produce very sparse contingency tables; the X-ray analysis has only 240 images and potentially rare findings. The manuscript does not report sparse-table diagnostics or handling, and it does not clearly identify which training, validation, or test observations enter causal discovery. Bootstrap repetition alone does not establish test calibration. Report these details and provide appropriate sensitivity evidence before interpreting stable orientations as reliable findings.

Necessary: repair the Shapley counterexample in Section 3.3 and Appendix A. Appendix A.2 leaves the allegedly unobserved Z3 fixed inside every coalition value, including the empty-coalition baseline. This does not establish what an estimator using only the observed variables would calculate after omitting Z3. Appendix A.1 also uses marginal replacement quantities that need to be distinguished from interventions on the stated SCM, where Z2 and Z3 cause Z1. Define a consistent estimand and observation model, then correct the derivation or remove the example. A zero local attribution also does not, by itself, imply absence of a population-level causal effect.

Necessary: narrow the validation claims. Intuitively plausible bird characteristics, clinically associated findings, and selected LIME/SHAP heatmaps do not independently verify the discovered causal relationships. The comparisons demonstrate differences in explanatory representation, but do not establish causal correctness. The real-data results should be presented as exploratory hypotheses under the stated assumptions unless additional evidence supports the stronger conclusions.

Optional: a comparison using the same macro-level annotations would help isolate the contribution of causal discovery from the interpretability supplied by those annotations. Releasing executable configurations and clarifying how multiple active bird attributes are consolidated would improve reproducibility; larger labels in Figure 8 would improve readability.
